Apicoplast and ER Proteomes (Quantitative)(Dd2)
Description: Description= BioID was used to perform large-scale identification of P. falciparum apicoplast proteins during asexual blood-stage growth. We achieved high positive predictive value of true apicoplast proteins by implementing an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) negative control to remove frequent contaminants expected based on the trafficking route of apicoplast proteins. Higher coverage was achieved by using the proteomic data set to develop an improved neural network prediction algorithm, ApicoPLAST Neural Network (PlastNN). The authors report a high-confidence apicoplast proteome of 346 proteins rich in novel and essential functions.For large-scale identification of apicoplast proteins, biotinylated proteins from late-stage BioIDâ€“Ap and BioIDâ€“ER parasites were purified using streptavidin-conjugated beads and identified by mass spectrometry. A total of 728 unique P. falciparum proteins were detected in the apicoplast and/or ER based on presence in at least 2 of 4 biological replicates and at least 2 unique spectral matches in any single mass spectrometry run. The abundance of each protein in apicoplast and ER samples was calculated by summing the total MS1 area of all matched peptides and normalizing to the total MS1 area of all detected P. falciparum peptides within each mass spectrometry run.

Study: Proteome and phosphoproteome during intraerythrocytic development (Quantitative)
Description: Description= Sample Preparation:Tightly synchronized ring (16 +/- 4 h postinvasion), trophozoites (26 +/- 4 h postinvasion), and schizonts (36 +/- 4 h postinvasion) were harvested, lysed with saponin, digested with LysC, labeled with one of 6 isobaric tags. The resulting peptides were fractionated into 20 fractions and either analyzed directly (global proteome) or enriched for phosphopeptides with immobilized metal affinity chromatography.Proteomic Analyses:Both phospho-enriched and nonphospho-enriched samples were analyzed via LC-MS/MS on an LTQ-Velos-Orbitrap mass spectrometer. Peptides were identified by matching individual MS/MS spectra with peptide sequences using Sequest. For phospho-enriched samples, individual phosphorylation sites on each peptide were scored to assess how confidently the modification could be localized to a single residue using AScore. Protein Quantification: Peptides matching each protein were grouped and their tandem mass tag (TMT) reporter ion intensities were scaled to a sum of 1.0. ANOVA was used to identify differentially expressed proteins based on the quantitation of individual peptides and Benjamini-Hochberg approach was used to correct for multiple hypothesis testing.
